PullRequest.Title: Unify new session and active session composer
PullRequest.Body:

The Agents window had two chat inputs. Running sessions used the workbench `ChatWidget` / `ChatInputPart`, while the new-session and new-chat composers used `NewChatInputWidget`: a separate implementation of about 4,600 lines with its own editor, attachments, completions, slash commands, paste handling, voice wiring and Send button. Every input feature had to be built twice, and anything that targets "the chat input" (keybindings, commands, accessibility) skipped the composer. That is how this started: the model picker keybindings did nothing before a session existed.

This PR deletes the separate composer. The new-session and new-chat composers now host the same `ChatWidget` as a running session, and only add what is specific to starting one.

## What we gain from unification

- **One input, one behavior.** The composer is a registered chat widget, so chat input commands and keybindings act on it: Send, Open Model Picker (Cmd+Alt+.), Switch to Next Model, Add Context, dictation, paste, focusing notices, and accessibility help. The keybinding bug is fixed by construction rather than with routing special cases.
- **Features come for free.** `#` references, agent host commands and skills, `/` commands, attachment pills, paste and drag and drop, input notices (tips, migrations, promotions), voice input and draft persistence all come from the shared input. Future chat input work reaches both surfaces without a port.
- **No more drift.** Model selection, send gating, slash commands and reference handling each have one implementation, so the composer can no longer quietly fall out of step with the running session's input.
- **Less code.** Product code is down 3,875 lines net (+1,863 / −5,738), and tests and fixtures are down 2,236. The old composer and its completion, paste and slash command handlers (about 4,600 lines) are replaced by about 1,000 lines of composer glue.

## How it works

- `SharedChatInputComposer` renders a `ChatWidget` bound to the draft session's chat model. The host still owns workspace selection, session creation and sending.
- `ChatWidget` / `ChatInputPart` gain small, generic host options, so an embedder can own parts of the input instead of forking it:
  - `submitHandler` + `hostSubmit`: the host sends, and decides when Send is enabled and how it is labeled.
  - `hostModelSelection`: the session provider owns the model; the input's model commands, picker and notifications act on it.
  - `deferredNotificationsEnabled`, `ownsDraftVoiceSession`, `menus.inputToolbar` and `inputPartHorizontalPadding`. `renderGettingStartedTip: false` now leaves the tip slot to the host.
- The Agents window pickers (agent, mode and permissions, model, session controls, busy state) are contributed to the input toolbar through `Menus.NewSessionChatInputToolbar` and action view items instead of being hand-built.
- What remains composer-specific: client-side slash commands run before the host sends, inline references are re-based for the trimmed prompt, attachments added before render are kept, and a draft-targeted Voice Mode session belongs to the composer (segmented control and decorations).
- File search for `github-remote-file` workspaces moves from an agent-host-specific provider to the generic `FileSystemFileSearchProvider`.

## Behavior changes for reviewers

- Status items render in the input's own status row, as in running sessions (below the input on phones).
- Add Context opens the workbench picker, and dictation uses the workbench command.
- The input chrome (Send button, input height) matches the running session's input. The blocks-ci hashes for the new-session fixtures are updated, and each changed image was compared against `main`.
- Pasted context that carries an icon, such as an issue picked from the workspace row, renders as its icon and name instead of "Pasted …".
- Removed: the `NewSessionConfig` and `NewSessionAttachContext` menus, and the old composer's custom OpenTelemetry status hover.

## How to test

In the Agents window:

1. In the new-session composer, Cmd+Alt+. opens the model picker, and **Chat: Switch to Next Model** changes the model.
2. `/models` opens the model picker and `/blobby` opens Customize Blobby, without starting a session. A `#` file reference is sent with the prompt.
3. Add Context, paste, Send, and Alt+Enter (send in the background) work.
4. In a running session, a new chat (Cmd+T) uses the same composer.
5. With `sessions.chat.experimental.newSessionComposerLayout` on, the controls move into the input, and the phone layout keeps the chip lane above the input.

Validation on `61d0cbc63b2`:

| Command | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `npm run typecheck-client` | Passed |
| `npm run eslint -- $(git diff --name-only --diff-filter=ACMR origin/main...HEAD -- '*.ts')` | Passed (49 files) |
| `node build/hygiene.ts $(git diff --name-only --diff-filter=ACMR origin/main...HEAD)` | Passed (58 files) |
| `npm run valid-layers-check` | Passed |
| `npm run check-cyclic-dependencies` | Passed |
| `./scripts/test.sh --runGlob '{vs/sessions/contrib/chat/test/**/*.test.js,vs/sessions/contrib/providers/agentHost/test/**/*.test.js,vs/workbench/contrib/chat/test/browser/widget/**/*.test.js,vs/workbench/contrib/chat/test/browser/voiceClient/*.test.js,vs/workbench/services/search/test/common/*.test.js}'` | Passed (5,913 passing, 25 pending) |
| Component fixtures (`sessions/` and `chat`), rendered in the component explorer | 3,614 of 3,616 render; the 2 `sessions/chatReferences` failures also fail on `main` |
| CI **Screenshots** check | Passed |

The changes were also checked live in Code OSS: model picker keybindings, Compare Models, slash commands, inline references, Add Context, send, the in-session composer, and the experimental layout toggle.

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: The observed element is explicitly auto-height and the synchronous call chain to input/list layout is direct. The exact frame cost varies by platform and toolbar contents.
Findings.PerformanceResource: Synchronous DOM/editor, toolbar, and hidden-list layout work
Findings.PerformanceScaling: A full ChatWidget layout is repeated whenever the auto-sized composer changes height, including wrapped/new input lines, attachment rows, notices, prompt animation wraps, and host width changes.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: Extra main-thread layout work on interactive input paths, causing typing/attachment jank and lower rendering throughput.
Findings.PreviousBehavior: The previous composer handled editor content-height changes by resizing and laying out its CodeEditorWidget, while viewport layout called the composer layout separately; it did not relayout a full chat widget/list when its intrinsic input height changed.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: The new observer watches the auto-height outer composer and calls _layoutWidget for every resize. _layoutWidget invokes ChatWidget.layout, which reruns ChatInputPart.layout and ChatListWidget.layout even when only the input's height changed.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: Added line 320 introduces an unfiltered ResizeObserver callback that performs whole-widget layout for both width and intrinsic height changes; no equivalent whole-widget callback existed in NewChatInputWidget.
Findings.Title: Restrict the composer resize observer to width changes
Findings.Impact: Typing until the prompt wraps, adding context pills, or showing a notice causes the already-laid-out ChatInputPart to be laid out again together with the hidden transcript surfaces.
Findings.Evidence: sharedChatInputComposer.css:14 gives .interactive-session height:auto, so input-height changes resize the observed container. The callback at line 320 calls _layoutWidget, which calls widget.layout. ChatWidget.layout (chatWidget.ts:4277-4295) runs inputPart.layout and list layout. ChatWidget's own input-height autorun explicitly calls only _layoutListForInputHeight and warns that re-entering inputPart.layout creates a layout loop (chatWidget.ts:2739-2752), but this outer observer bypasses that safeguard.
Findings.Recommendation: Track the last measured width and call widget.layout only when width changes (or rely on the host layout callback); let ChatWidget's existing input-height path update list-side sizing without re-entering ChatInputPart.layout.

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: The changed constructor and unconditional transitive render path are explicit. Exact milliseconds and retained bytes vary by registered renderers/contributions, which affects severity but not the mechanism.
Findings.PerformanceResource: ChatListWidget DOM, list renderers, widget contributions, listeners, and retained objects
Findings.PerformanceScaling: The cost is paid once for every new-session or new-chat view and remains retained for each hidden view kept in the sessions grid.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: Higher Agents window/new-chat creation latency and increased retained memory/GC pressure.
Findings.PreviousBehavior: The removed NewChatInputWidget created only the composer editor, attachments, notices, pickers, and related input services; it did not construct a chat transcript list.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: Each composer now instantiates and renders a full ChatWidget. ChatWidget.render unconditionally calls createList to construct ChatListWidget and then instantiates every ChatWidget.CONTRIBS entry, while the new CSS merely hides .interactive-list and the welcome DOM. The composer also marks the widget visible even when inputVisible later hides its container.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: Added line 213 replaces the former input-only NewChatInputWidget with a full ChatWidget instance; the old composer path had no ChatListWidget construction.
Findings.Title: Add an input-only render path instead of constructing a hidden transcript
Findings.Impact: Opening the Agents window or adding a new-session/new-chat view synchronously builds a transcript/list subsystem that this surface can never display; retaining multiple hidden views retains one such object graph per view.
Findings.Evidence: The added createInstance(ChatWidget) at line 213 reaches ChatWidget.render, which unconditionally invokes createList (chatWidget.ts:1214); createList constructs ChatListWidget and its renderer/event graph (chatWidget.ts:2316-2350), and render then maps all ChatWidget.CONTRIBS (chatWidget.ts:1295). sharedChatInputComposer.css:8-15 only applies display:none/auto sizing, so it does not avoid this construction. NewChatView constructs and renders this composer for each new-session/new-chat view (chatView.ts:157-161).
Findings.Recommendation: Add a ChatWidget input-only option that still creates/registers ChatInputPart but skips welcome/transcript DOM, ChatListWidget/renderers, transcript listeners, and contributions that are not input-related; also propagate host visibility instead of permanently calling setVisible(true).

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: The registration-to-network call path and per-ignore-file cardinality are explicit; only repository ignore-file count varies.
Findings.PerformanceScaling: Cold search makes one blob request per .gitignore or .ignore across the remote tree; recursive visits let reads overlap. Warm cache-key searches reuse enumeration.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: Excessive network calls and increased cold search latency.
Findings.PreviousBehavior: No GitHub file-search provider was registered, so file search made no ignore-file blob calls.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: The registration routes GitHub searches through a recursive walker that reads every encountered ignore file through GitHubFileSystemProvider.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: Added line 34 registers the recursive provider for github-remote-file, introducing this network fan-out on GitHub search paths.
Findings.Title: Throttle GitHub ignore-file reads
Findings.Impact: Quick Open, Add Context, or #file on a remote monorepo can wait on dozens of GitHub blob downloads and consume API rate limits.
Findings.Evidence: FileSystemFileSearchProvider limits only readdir (lines 106-118); ignore readFile calls are outside that limiter (121-128) while recursive visits overlap. GitHubFileSystemProvider.readFile (245-256) calls content.getBlob.
Findings.Recommendation: Bound ignore-file reads with a shared network limiter and coalesce/cache immutable blobs by SHA while preserving ignore semantics and cancellation.

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: Allocation cardinality and cache lifetime are explicit. Exact heap size depends on repository path lengths and number of refs visited.
Findings.PerformanceResource: Retained tuple arrays, basename strings, directory arrays, and map entries
Findings.PerformanceScaling: Each fetched tree now retains one additional tuple and basename string per repository entry plus one children array/map entry per directory; total retained memory grows with the summed entry counts of every distinct owner/repo/ref accessed during the workbench lifetime.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: Increased retained heap and GC pressure after opening large cloud repositories or multiple branches.
Findings.PreviousBehavior: The cache retained one entries Map for each recursive GitHub tree and readdir scanned that map; stat/readFile did not create a second per-entry index.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: Every cold tree fetch now eagerly allocates a children Map and pushes a newly allocated [basename, FileType] tuple for every entry, even when the caller only requested stat or readFile. treeCache has no size bound or timed eviction: fetchedAt controls freshness on a later lookup, but old keys are removed only on account change or provider disposal.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: Added line 208 creates and retains one new tuple and substring per cached tree entry; this materially increases the size of the pre-existing unbounded per-ref cache.
Findings.Title: Bound or lazily build the cached child index
Findings.Impact: A large repository pays the duplicate index cost on first file access, and switching among repositories/refs accumulates all duplicate indices until the workbench/provider is disposed.
Findings.Evidence: The added loop at lines 196-209 visits the complete entries map and line 208 allocates the per-entry basename/tuple retained by cacheEntry at line 211. treeCache is keyed by owner/repo/ref (line 48), fetchTree only tests TTL without deleting unrelated/stale keys (lines 130-143), and clearCaches is only called for client changes/disposal (lines 293-302).
Findings.Recommendation: Keep the O(1) readdir optimization but build the child index lazily on first readdir/search (so stat/readFile do not pay it), use a more compact representation where possible, and evict tree entries with a bounded LRU or actual TTL cleanup.

RegressionFixes.Mechanism: The old readdir implementation scanned the complete recursive entries Map and tested/sliced every path for each directory listing, making browsing D directories in an N-entry repository O(D*N).
RegressionFixes.Symptom: Expanding directories in large github-remote-file repositories repeatedly rescanned the full tree, increasing directory-open latency and CPU with both repository size and the number of directories visited.
RegressionFixes.FixedBehavior: The PR builds a parent-to-direct-children index once per fetched tree and changes readdir to a direct lookup/copy, reducing repeated listings to O(number of returned children) after the O(N) index build.
RegressionFixes.Evidence: Base line 229 is the loop over all tree.entries inside readdir, introduced by the blamed commit. Added line 241 returns only tree.children.get(path); the new index is constructed once when the already-recursive tree is fetched and shared by subsequent readdir calls.

Scenarios.Scenario: Open or retain a new-session/new-chat composer in the Agents window
Scenarios.CriticalPath: NewChatView constructs NewChatWidget/NewChatInSessionWidget, which synchronously renders SharedChatInputComposer and a full ChatWidget before the composer is usable. Draft-model acquisition starts afterward; local placeholder creation is in-memory and off the initial synchronous render once scheduled.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of new-session/new-chat views retained in the sessions grid; one ChatWidget, hidden transcript list, renderer graph, and contribution set per view.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Construction is synchronous on the UI thread per rendered view. Draft rebindings cancel the previous CancellationTokenSource so only the latest binding is authoritative.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Chat model references are reused when the bound resource is unchanged; a missing/unloadable draft falls back to a local model. Transcript/list construction has no lazy or shared cache and is paid per composer, including views later hidden by inputVisible.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the diff directly instantiates ChatWidget, and ChatWidget.render unconditionally constructs ChatListWidget and all registered contributions despite CSS hiding the transcript.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Exact startup milliseconds and retained bytes depend on registered renderers/contributions and the number of grid views users retain.
Scenarios.Verdict: Reportable eager-work regression: an input-only surface constructs and retains full transcript infrastructure; host visibility is not propagated to ChatWidget.

Scenarios.Scenario: Type, wrap text, add attachments, or show notices in the shared composer
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Input/attachment/notice DOM changes resize the auto-height composer; its new ResizeObserver synchronously calls ChatWidget.layout, which lays out ChatInputPart and the hidden list before the frame can complete.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of intrinsic height changes, driven by wrapped/new lines, attachment rows, notices, and prompt-option animation; width changes can also cause both host layout and observer layout.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: All work is serialized on the browser main thread. ResizeObserver batches notifications, but each delivered resize invokes whole-widget layout without checking whether width changed.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No coalescing or width equality guard exists in the added observer. ChatWidget already has a specialized input-height path that avoids re-entering ChatInputPart.layout.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: auto-height CSS and the direct ResizeObserver -> _layoutWidget -> ChatWidget.layout call chain are explicit.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Frame cost varies with editor/toolbars and platform, but the redundant synchronous layout is present on every relevant height transition.
Scenarios.Verdict: Reportable synchronous-layout regression; restrict the observer to width changes and leave intrinsic-height handling to ChatWidget.

Scenarios.Scenario: Cold and warm file search over a github-remote-file workspace (Quick Open, Add Context, or #file)
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The new search-provider registration recursively enumerates the remote tree before returning matches. A cold tree requires one GitHub Trees API request; every encountered .gitignore/.ignore then requires a GitHub Blob API request, and the query awaits all recursive visits. Warm cache-key searches reuse the collected URI list.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Fetch the complete recursive Git tree
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One per cold owner/repo/ref, coalesced across concurrent callers and reused for five minutes.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The filesystem provider already fetched the full tree for stat/readdir/readFile.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Must complete before the first directory enumeration and search traversal can progress.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Fetch and decode each .gitignore/.ignore blob encountered by recursive file search
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: K requests for K encountered ignore files on cold enumeration; cache-key reuse avoids repetition only after the full file list is cached.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: No file-search provider was registered for github-remote-file, so search made no ignore-file blob requests.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: All reads are awaited before fileSearch returns and can burst outside the readdir limiter.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: N repository entries, D directories visited after excludes, and K nested ignore files. Boundary cardinality is one cold recursive-tree request plus K cold blob reads; in-process readdir cardinality is D.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: readdir is limited to 16, but ignore-file readFile/getBlob calls occur outside that limiter across concurrent recursive visits, so aggregate network concurrency is not bounded by the traversal limiter.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: GitHub tree fetches are positively cached for five minutes, negatively cached for one minute, and coalesced per owner/repo/ref. FileSystemFileSearchProvider coalesces a folder enumeration by cacheKey and removes failed entries; clearCache drops it. Ignore blob contents are not cached/coalesced by GitHubFileSystemProvider.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: registration, recursive traversal, default ignore-file semantics, and getBlob boundary are directly traced.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: K varies from zero in small repositories to dozens or hundreds in monorepos; network latency and API limits vary by account/location.
Scenarios.Verdict: Reportable boundary fan-out/concurrency regression; throttle and coalesce immutable ignore-blob reads.

Scenarios.Scenario: Stat, read, browse, and search across large GitHub repositories and multiple refs
Scenarios.CriticalPath: On a cold owner/repo/ref, getTree returns all N entries, then the changed code synchronously builds a second parent-to-children index before stat/readdir/readFile can continue. readFile subsequently fetches one requested blob. Warm tree access skips rebuilding until TTL expiry for the same key.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One coalesced request per cold owner/repo/ref; warm for five minutes.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same recursive tree request occurred, but only the entries map was constructed.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The response and O(N) index build must finish before filesystem operations proceed.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One per readFile call; no provider-level positive blob cache.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same blob operation existed before the PR.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Required only for file content reads, not stat/readdir.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: N entries per recursive tree and the summed N across every distinct owner/repo/ref accessed. Directory browsing performs D readdir calls, now direct child lookups rather than D full-tree scans.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: pendingFetches coalesces concurrent tree loads per key. Index construction is synchronous after each cold response. Distinct keys can load independently; treeCache has no global size bound.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The tree freshness TTL is checked only when that same key is accessed again; unrelated stale keys are not evicted. Cache clearing occurs on account/client changes or provider disposal. The child index is built eagerly even for stat/readFile and retained with the entries map.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: per-entry allocation and cache lifetime are explicit; the old full-map readdir loop and new direct lookup also prove the CPU optimization.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Heap growth depends on repository path lengths, repository size, and how many repositories/branches a session visits.
Scenarios.Verdict: Reportable materially amplified retention from the duplicate per-entry index. The PR also fixes the prior O(D*N) repeated readdir scan; that fix was recorded separately and should be preserved with lazy/compact indexing and bounded cache eviction.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over the full 75-file inventory and relevant production/test hunks. Submitted four diff-caused findings: eager hidden transcript construction, redundant whole-widget resize layout, per-ignore-file GitHub network fan-out, and materially amplified unbounded tree-cache retention. Also recorded the verified O(D*N) readdir regression fix against its blamed introducing commit.

Stats.CostNote: Copilot SDK reports nano-AI units and model billing multipliers; it does not provide a USD conversion.
